extracted.intended_audience: companies using AI in marketing; in-house counsel; compliance and marketing teams
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for businesses on how to lawfully market products and services that reference or use artificial intelligence in light of FTC enforcement priorities. Focuses on what claims trigger scrutiny and practical steps (audits, documentation, training) to reduce regulatory and reputational risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantiate every claim (explicit and implicit)
rubrics_metrics.description: Companies using AI in their marketing must be able to substantiate every claim they make, both explicit and implicit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gather and document evidence proving each claim; if you claim your AI improves client outcomes by 50%, you must have reliable data to back it up. Treat implicit suggestions of capability or benefit as claims that require proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance & efficacy — tool must perform as advertised
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the AI tool perform as advertised?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Truth-in-advertising requires demonstrable proof of performance. Examples from enforcement: Workado advertised 98% accuracy but testing showed 53%; Click Profit and others promised automated systems producing thousands per month but customer outcomes did not support those claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lawful purpose — product must not be sold to enable deception
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the AI tool being sold for a lawful purpose or to enable deception?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marketing or offering tools intended to generate false testimonials, fake reviews, or otherwise facilitate consumer deception can violate the FTC Act (example: Rytr alleged to facilitate fake online testimonials). Avoid promoting uses that enable unlawful or deceptive conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Income & earnings claims must be truthful and substantiated
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid promising financial success or a specific return on investment based on AI capabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims that an AI product will generate specific earnings (e.g., 'tens of thousands of dollars' or 'thousands a month') must be supported by reliable evidence and clearly communicable to the average consumer. The FTC has targeted companies making baseless get-rich-quick style claims (Ascent Ecom, Click Profit).

rubrics_metrics.name: Authenticity of sample outputs — examples must be genuine
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the examples of your AI’s output (e.g., AI-generated images or text) genuine and not deceptively edited?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not present edited or manipulated examples as representative results. Ensure any demo content is authentic, clearly labeled, and not misleading about typical outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not misrepresent AI capabilities (avoid hyperbole/equivalence to humans)
rubrics_metrics.description: Companies must not overstate the capabilities of the AI itself (e.g., claiming an AI is equivalent to or better than human professionals without validation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: marketing an AI as 'the world’s first robot lawyer' without testing against human lawyer performance drew FTC scrutiny. Claims comparing AI to human performance should be validated by appropriate comparative testing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy claims require robust validation
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific accuracy or effectiveness percentages in marketing must be validated by reliable testing and data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you advertise metrics such as '98% accurate,' maintain and be able to produce test results and methodology demonstrating that accuracy. The FTC challenged Workado’s 98% accuracy claim when internal testing showed ~53%.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat 'AI' as a compliance red flag — use clear, precise language
rubrics_metrics.description: Using the term 'AI' in marketing places greater scrutiny on your product and language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure claims are not only technically true but are clear and not susceptible to misinterpretation by the average consumer. Avoid vague, sensational, or ambiguous wording that could be construed as deceptive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct a comprehensive marketing audit
rubrics_metrics.description: Review all public-facing materials to identify and evaluate every AI-related claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audit websites, social media, sales scripts, advertisements, and partner materials to catalog explicit and implicit AI claims. This is the first step to identifying statements that need substantiation or revision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document evidence and be prepared for compliance monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain documentation proving the veracity of claims and be ready for potential enforcement oversight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect datasets, test methodologies, user outcome statistics, and internal analyses showing claims are supported. Enforcement outcomes can include compliance orders requiring monitoring and notice to consumers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Train marketing and sales teams on precise, substantiated language
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure anyone speaking for the company understands the importance of accurate and provable statements about AI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide training so marketers and salespeople avoid unsupported claims and understand documentation requirements; institute approval processes for AI-related messaging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid facilitating deceptive content or uses
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not market AI tools for purposes that promote or enable deceptive consumer-facing content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly prohibit and avoid advertising use-cases such as generating fake testimonials, deceptive review manipulation, or other applications designed to mislead consumers—these uses have been targeted by the FTC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipate investigations and resource impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Be aware that FTC inquiries and enforcement actions require substantial legal work and can carry significant penalties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proactive compliance (audits, documentation, training) reduces risk of investigations, multimillion-dollar penalties, injunctions, and reputational harm. The agency has pursued enforcement across industries, signaling broad applicability of these standards.
